lines: I remember your hands at the edge of the dark. Stronger than any plate I have hammered.
The forge sounded like home again after you brought me back.
You returned my name to me when I could barely remember it.
I can work the bellows without hearing that old hunger now.
You gave me another morning and the strength to notice it.
My hands remember the hammer because you stayed long enough to help.
I owe you more than a discount. I am still finding the proper shape for that debt.
The village welcomed me home, but you made home possible.
I remember your face becoming clear while everything else was still fog.
You did not run when I gave you every reason to.
The cure gave me my life back. Your courage carried it to me.
I can stand beside my neighbors without fearing what I might do.
Do not make a ceremony of it. Just know that I remember.
Every ordinary day at the forge feels borrowed from your kindness.
You repaired something no hammer could reach.
I thought the person I was had been lost. You proved me wrong.
Some part of me still listens for that old <shake>groan</shake>. I hate that part.
I checked my old apron this morning. Even that felt like a gift.
When armor saves a life, I trust the work. You saved mine without any armor.
I am glad you are here to hear me say thank you properly.
I know your face, but the memory rings like a dented helm.
There was iron in my mouth, or fear, or both. Then I remember you.
Parts of that night return out of order. You are in every version.
I think you helped me, though the memory keeps slipping at the edges.
Your voice sounds familiar in a way I cannot place yet.
I woke near the forge with your face already lodged in my thoughts.
Did you stand beside me through all of it? I remember someone refusing to leave.
The others say I should thank you. My own memory is slowly agreeing.
I can recall the cure, but not whether I fought you before it worked.
Something in me recognizes you before my mind catches up.
I remember cold stone, a sharp taste, and your hands keeping steady.
My old life came back in pieces. Your name has not found its piece yet.
I know I was dangerous. I do not know how close you had to stand.
The fog lifts when you speak, then settles again.
Forgive the staring. I am trying to fit your face to the right memory.
I believe you saved me. I wish belief and memory were the same thing.
The hammer feels familiar. Gratitude still feels new.
If I ask the same question twice, give the answer time to hold.
You seem safe, even when the old fear tells me nothing is.
I may understand what you did before I remember all of it.
I remember you through cracked mail and bad dreams. Stand where I can see your hands.
I know you helped. I also remember why my hands still shake.
The cure left echoes behind. Stand where I can breathe around them.
I still need a little distance.
My body expects danger that is gone.
Please warn me before coming closer.
Gratitude and fear can exist together.
The cure worked before the fear faded.
Open space helps me breathe.
The memory does not listen to reason.
Seeing you still makes me shake.
Give me time to sort your face.
Do not take my caution for anger.
Some nights still feel wrong.
I believe what the others told me.
The old hunger left a shadow.
I am learning to trust this room.
I can thank you from here.
I want to remember you kindly.
Today is easier than yesterday.
